Elle dispose d’un patrimoine historique riche (romain, amazigh, arabe), d’une culture authentique, et d’une forte identité nationale. Ses ressources énergétiques, sa stabilité territoriale, et son potentiel touristique encore préservé en font un pays à fort avenir. 🇬🇧 English Algeria is an attractive country thanks to its unique natural diversity, from the Mediterranean coast to the Sahara Desert. Its preserved tourism potential and strategic position make it a country of long-term interest. 🇪🇸 Español Argelia es un país atractivo por su gran diversidad natural, desde el Mediterráneo hasta el Sahara. Proud Algerian 🇩🇿🔥/  First national edit ig ————————————— The history of Algeria spans thousands of years, evolving from the ancient indigenous Numidian kingdoms united by King Massinissa in 202 BCE through centuries of rich Mediterranean civilization. During the classical era, the region produced towering intellectual figures of global significance, including Apuleius of Madaurus, a Platonist philosopher and the author of The Golden Ass—hailed as the world's first complete surviving Latin novel—and Saint Augustine of Hippo, one of the most influential Christian philosophers and theologians in Western history. Following antiquity, Algeria became a vibrant cradle for major Islamic dynasties that reshaped the Mediterranean. The Fatimid Caliphate originated from the Kutama Berbers in the mountains of Ikjan (Mila, Algeria) in 909 CE before expanding its empire and establishing Cairo. Later, the region witnessed the rise of the Almohad Caliphate (Al-Muwahhidun), founded by Ibn Tumart from the Masmuda tribes, who initiated a profound religious and political movement from North Africa that united the Maghreb and al-Andalus. The region also saw the rule of the Rustamids, Ziyanids, and the formidable maritime sovereignty of the Regency of Algiers. In the face of the French invasion launched in 1830, Algerians waged a fierce, prolonged resistance led by iconic figures such as Emir Abdelkader, who established a modern state, and legendary commanders like Lalla Fatma N'Soumer and Tariq ibn Ziyad from earlier centuries. This unbroken legacy of defiance ultimately culminated in the historic War of Independence and the birth of the People's Democratic Republic of Algeria in 1962, with Ahmed Ben Bella serving as its first president. #history #algeria #fyp #culture
